context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous claim processing. It couples a cloud-hosted web interface with asynchronous integration patterns to decouple users from legacy system lag.

## Key Elements
* External Users: Customers, Brokers, and Claims Adjusters
* New Claims Platform: Azure App Service web application hosted in Azure West Europe
* Integration Layer: Azure API Management Gateway and Azure Service Bus
* System of Record: On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe

## Relationships
* Customers and Brokers interact with the New Claims Platform via HTTPS for online claim submission
* Claims Adjusters interact with the New Claims Platform via HTTPS for claim handling
* New Claims Platform interacts with the Legacy Mainframe via REST/HTTPS for synchronous queries through the API Gateway
* New Claims Platform interacts with the Legacy Mainframe via AMQP/HTTPS using Azure Service Bus for asynchronous claim state updates
* Services authenticate against Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) using OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.0

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Provider: Hybrid (On-premise mainframe and Azure West Europe)
* Compute & Hosting: Azure App Service for containerized web applications
* Integration & Messaging: Azure API Management Gateway and Azure Service Bus with Dead-Letter Queues
* Security & Identity: Azure Active Directory (Entra ID), Azure Key Vault, and TLS 1.3 with mTLS
* Infrastructure & Observability: Azure Bicep/Terraform and Azure Application Insights

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed Azure services to offset the team's low cloud experience while enforcing strict security boundaries. An asynchronous integration layer and API gateway isolate the new platform from legacy mainframe lag and protect fragile quarterly interface constraints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization Platform]
[Core Purpose: Gradually replaces a legacy mainframe claims system while maintaining parallel operations and compliance over a 3-year migration window.]

## Key Elements
- Users: Customer, Broker, Claims Adjuster, Business Operations / Migration Manager
- External Systems: On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe
- Cloud Infrastructure: Azure West Europe (VNet with Private Endpoints)
- Gateways & Routing: Azure API Management
- Compute Containers: Azure Container Apps (Java / Spring Boot for Claims Processing Service, React / Node.js for Migration Dashboard)
- Integration & Messaging: Azure Service Bus, Azure Logic Apps / Functions
- Data & Storage: Azure SQL Database
- Security & Observability: Azure Key Vault, Azure Active Directory (Entra ID), Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker -> Azure API Management: Online claim submission via HTTPS / REST
- Claims Adjuster / Migration Manager -> Azure API Management: Web application access via HTTPS / OAuth 2.0 (OpenID Connect)
- Azure API Management -> Azure Container Apps: Dynamic claim-type routing via internal VNet
- Azure Container Apps -> Azure SQL Database: ACID-compliant transaction persistence via TDS
- Azure Container Apps -> Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous event publishing and queuing
- Azure Service Bus -> On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe: Hybrid integration bridge via TLS 1.3 / mTLS and Site-to-Site VPN / ExpressRoute
- Azure Container Apps -> Azure Key Vault: Managed Identity secret retrieval

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Selected for dynamic feature-flag routing to guarantee R-06 one-day rollbacks per claim type without mainframe changes
- Java / Spring Boot on Azure Container Apps: Chosen for enterprise maturity to support teams with low cloud experience
- Azure SQL Database: Mandated for ACID compliance to satisfy R-04 (no lost or double-processed claims)
- Azure Service Bus & Logic Apps: Utilized for asynchronous queueing around the strict nightly batch window (23:00-05:00)
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): Implements SSO for R-07 security compliance
- Terraform / Bicep: Mandated as Infrastructure as Code for repeatable hybrid deployments

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples modern cloud workloads from the legacy mainframe via API Management and asynchronous messaging, satisfying strict constraints like batch windows and limited cloud experience.]
[It ensures zero data loss and rapid rollbacks through isolated domain services, robust ACID storage, and secure VNet connectivity.]

Azure API Management.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe while ensuring continuous processing. It utilizes Azure cloud services integrated with an on-premise mainframe to enable seamless claim migrations and low-latency adjuster workflows.

## Key Elements
- Azure API Management (APIM): Internal VNet mode gateway acting as the single secure entry point.
- Azure Application Gateway with WAF: Fronts APIM to inspect incoming traffic for threats.
- Claims Processing Service: Java, Spring Boot service hosted in Azure Container Apps.
- Migration Dashboard: React, Node.js container application for migration management.
- On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe: System of record connected via Azure Logic Apps and Azure Functions.
- Supporting Azure Services: Azure Service Bus, Azure SQL Database (TDS), Azure Key Vault, Azure Active Directory (Entra ID), Azure Application Insights.

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker -> Azure Application Gateway: Online claim submission via HTTPS / REST.
- Claims Adjuster -> Azure Application Gateway: Web application access via HTTPS / OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect.
- Azure Application Gateway -> Azure API Management: Secure traffic forwarding via internal VNet.
- Azure API Management -> Claims Processing Service: Dynamic claim-type routing via internal VNet using mTLS.
- Azure API Management -> Migration Dashboard: Dashboard traffic routing via internal VNet using mTLS.
- Azure API Management -> Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): JWT token validation via OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect.
- Azure API Management -> Azure Application Insights: Telemetry and metrics publishing via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management (Standard/Premium): Selected as the API gateway for routing and rate limiting.
- Azure Container Apps: Hosts microservices with low cloud operational overhead.
- Java & Spring Boot: Core runtime for modern claim processing logic.
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): Enforces Single Sign-On (SSO) and OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect.
- Bicep / Terraform & GitOps: Implements Infrastructure as Code for reliable deployments and rollbacks.
- Mutual TLS (mTLS) & Azure Key Vault: Secures service-to-service communication and secret management.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects the fragile, expensive-to-change on-premise mainframe while incrementally migrating claim types to the cloud. Leveraging managed Azure services minimizes operational complexity for a team with limited cloud experience while meeting strict security, consistency, and fallback requirements.

Claims Processing Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform via a hybrid architecture, gradually replacing the legacy mainframe while ensuring continuous processing.]

## Key Elements
- Azure API Management
- Claims Processing Service (Java, Spring Boot, Azure Container Apps)
- Azure SQL Database
- Azure Service Bus
- Azure Key Vault
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Azure API Management -> Claims Processing Service: Dynamic claim-type routing [HTTPS / VNet]
- Claims Processing Service -> Azure SQL Database: ACID-compliant transaction persistence and outbox pattern [TDS]
- Claims Processing Service -> Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous event publishing [AMQP]
- Claims Processing Service -> Azure Key Vault: Secret and credential retrieval [HTTPS / Managed Identity]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Chosen for simple container orchestration suited to low cloud experience teams.
- Spring Boot: Selected for opinionated microservice boilerplate and robust ecosystem integration.
- Azure SQL Database: Provides reliable relational persistence with local outbox table support for R-04.
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breakers and caching adapters to mitigate mainframe latency (R-05).
- Azure Active Directory: Enforces OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect Single Sign-On (R-07).

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture decouples frontend clients from the legacy mainframe via API Management, enabling seamless, gradual claim-type migration within 3 years. Utilizing managed Azure services and standard enterprise patterns (Outbox, Circuit Breaker) minimizes operational risk for a team with limited cloud experience.]

Migration Dashboard.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe with a modern Azure cloud platform. Its core purpose is to enable incremental claim type migration and secure claims management while maintaining continuous legacy operations.]

## Key Elements
- Migration Project Managers and Operations Leads
- Migration Dashboard (React, Node.js, Azure Container Apps)
- Rollback Controller Component
- Reconciliation Viewer Component & Data Aggregator
- RBAC & Authorization Middleware
- Audit Logging Service
- Azure SQL Database
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
- Azure Key Vault
- Azure Logic Apps

## Relationships
- Migration Project Managers -> Migration Dashboard: Accesses via Azure API Management [HTTPS / OIDC / OAuth 2.0]
- Rollback Controller -> Claims Processing Service: Triggers feature flag switches [HTTP/REST]
- Reconciliation Viewer & Data Aggregator -> Azure SQL Database: Queries reconciliation metrics and audit logs [TDS / TLS 1.3]
- Migration Dashboard -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieves secrets [Managed Identity / HTTPS]
- Azure Logic Apps -> On-premise Mainframe: Polls legacy status [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React: Frontend UI framework for the Migration Dashboard due to team familiarity and component reusability
- Node.js: Backend runtime for handling API requests, RBAC middleware, and reconciliation aggregation
- Azure Container Apps: Serverless container hosting platform minimizing infrastructure management for a cloud-novice team
- Azure SQL Database: Relational datastore for audit logs and reconciliation metrics, accessed via TDS
- Bicep & GitHub Actions: IaC and GitOps pipeline for repeatable, auditable deployments given low cloud experience

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture bridges the legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe and modern cloud services using Azure Container Apps and API Management. It ensures safety-critical governance through RBAC, immutable audit logging, and rapid rollback controls to satisfy strict compliance and low-risk migration constraints.]

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform designed to gradually replace a 30-year-old legacy mainframe while maintaining continuous operations. Its core purpose is to decouple online claim submissions and adjuster workflows from the legacy system using Azure-native cloud services.

## Key Elements
- Azure Service Bus (Premium Tier)
- Claims Processing Service (Java, Spring Boot, Azure Container Apps)
- Migration Dashboard (React, Node.js, Azure Container Apps)
- Service Bus Management API Wrapper (Azure Functions)
- On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
- Azure Key Vault
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Claims Processing Service -> Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous event publishing and queuing [AMQP 1.0, TLS 1.3]
- Azure Service Bus -> On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe: Hybrid integration buffer and batch processing [TLS 1.3, mTLS, ExpressRoute/VPN]
- Migration Dashboard -> Service Bus Management API Wrapper: DLQ monitoring and message triage [HTTPS, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC]
- Service Bus Management API Wrapper -> Azure Service Bus: Queue management and scoped message replay [Azure SDK, Azure RBAC via Managed Identities]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus Premium: Provides dedicated resources, geo-disaster recovery, and native AMQP 1.0 support suitable for teams with low cloud experience.
- AMQP 1.0 Protocol: Enables reliable, cross-platform messaging and competing consumers pattern.
- Azure RBAC & Managed Identities: Replaces SAS keys to enforce least-privilege access across services.
- Azure Private Endpoints: Restricts network perimeter security by prohibiting public internet access to the broker.
- Azure Functions (.NET): Implements the secure management API wrapper without custom infrastructure overhead.
- Terraform / Bicep: Mandated for Infrastructure as Code to prevent manual configuration drift.

## Rationale
This architecture fits the requirements by utilizing a robust, managed hybrid messaging backbone that isolates the expensive legacy mainframe from modern cloud-native components. The use of Azure Service Bus Premium guarantees zero data loss (NFR-04) and handles the strict nightly batch window constraints while supporting the required one-day fallback switch (NFR-06).

Azure Logic Apps / Functions.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining zero downtime and strict data consistency during a 3-year migration.]

## Key Elements
* Customer and Broker
* Claims Adjuster
* Claims Operations Manager
* On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe
* Azure API Management
* Claims Processing Service (Java, Spring Boot, Azure Container Apps)
* Migration Dashboard (React, Node.js, Azure Container Apps)
* Azure Service Bus
* Azure Logic Apps / Functions (Inbound Integration Workflow, Mainframe Sync Function, Operations Telemetry Forwarder, Exception Triage Orchestrator, Replay & Audit API)
* Azure SQL Database
* Azure Key Vault
* Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
* Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
* Customer and Broker submit claims to Azure API Management via HTTPS/TLS 1.3.
* Claims Adjuster interacts with Claims Processing Service and Migration Dashboard via HTTPS.
* Azure API Management routes requests to Claims Processing Service and Azure Service Bus using HTTPS/AMQP.
* Mainframe Sync Function communicates with On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe using HTTPS/TCP/SNA with mTLS.
* Replay & Audit API connects to Azure Service Bus to securely push deduplicated messages using AMQP.
* Azure Logic Apps / Functions securely retrieve secrets from Azure Key Vault via Managed Identities.

## Technology Stack
* Azure Container Apps: Hosts microservices providing serverless container scaling with minimal cloud expertise required.
* Azure Service Bus: Manages asynchronous message queuing to guarantee zero lost or duplicated claims (R-04).
* C# .NET 8 Isolated Worker: Powers Azure Functions for robust protocol adaptation within the 5-second timeout window.
* Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): Enforces OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect Single Sign-On and RBAC.
* Azure Key Vault: Secures connection strings and encryption keys via Managed Identities.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture abstracts complex legacy integration protocols using managed Azure services, minimizing operational overhead for a cloud-novice team. It strictly enforces business continuity requirements by isolating the fragile mainframe and providing robust exception handling, idempotency, and audit trails.]

Azure SQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
Gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid cloud platform. The system ensures continuous claim processing while migrating claim types over a three-year period.

## Key Elements
- Customer, Broker, Claims Adjuster
- On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe
- Azure API Management
- Claims Processing Service (Java, Spring Boot, Azure Container Apps)
- Migration Dashboard (React, Node.js, Azure Container Apps)
- Azure SQL Database (Serverless tier avoided; Provisioned Tier, Gen5 hardware, `azure-westeurope`)
- Internal Database Schemas: Claim Operational Store, Migration State & Routing Registry, Audit & Reconciliation Log
- Azure Service Bus
- Azure Logic Apps / Functions
- Azure Key Vault
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Claims Processing Service -> Azure SQL Database: CRUD operations and high-frequency lookups using Tabular Data Stream (TDS) over TLS 1.3 via Azure Private Link
- Azure SQL Database -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieval of Customer-Managed Keys for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) via HTTPS (REST) over VNet service endpoint
- Azure SQL Database -> Azure Application Insights: Streaming audit logs and performance metrics using native diagnostic settings
- Users -> Azure API Management: API requests via HTTPS (REST) / OpenID Connect

## Technology Stack
- Azure SQL Database: ACID-compliant persistence, data consistency, and sub-2-second adjuster screen loads
- Provisioned Tier Compute (Gen5 hardware): Prevents cold-start latencies associated with serverless architectures
- Microsoft Entra ID: Single Sign-On and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), disabling local SQL authentication
- Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with Customer-Managed Keys: Data protection at rest via Azure Key Vault
- Flyway / Liquibase: Automated schema migration management for hybrid coexistence

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture maintains the legacy mainframe as the system of record while incrementally offloading claim types to an Azure-hosted platform, strictly satisfying the three-year coexistence constraint. Using a provisioned Azure SQL Database with private endpoints guarantees low-latency performance, robust security, and rapid one-day rollback capabilities.

    description: "Logs migration state transitions and reconciliation events"

Azure Key Vault.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous claim processing. It secures sensitive financial data and credentials using Azure Key Vault with zero-trust architecture.

## Key Elements
- Secrets Management Component
- Keys Management Component
- Access Control Component
- Caching & Event Listener Component
- Claims Processing Service
- Migration Dashboard
- Azure SQL Database
- Azure Key Vault Managed HSM

## Relationships
- Claims Processing Service -> Secrets Management Component: Retrieves connection strings via Azure SDK over HTTPS (REST) via Azure Private Endpoint
- Azure SQL Database -> Keys Management Component: Performs Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) operations via Azure internal secure channel
- Claims Processing Service & Migration Dashboard -> Access Control Component: Authenticates using Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) Managed Identities

## Technology Stack
- Azure Key Vault: Centralized secret and credential management to mitigate limited cloud experience
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): Zero-trust, credential-free authentication via Managed Identities
- Azure Key Vault Managed HSM: Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for cryptographic sovereignty over sensitive data
- Azure Private Endpoints: Secures data-in-transit by blocking public internet access
- In-memory short-TTL cache (5-15 minutes): Balances performance (R-05) and security against transient outages

## Rationale
This architecture secures sensitive PII and financial data while protecting operational availability during a 3-year hybrid migration. Fully managed Azure primitives and private networking mitigate the team's limited cloud experience.

Azure Active Directory (Entra ID).analysis:
## Overview
[Hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization Platform gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native platform using Azure services. It enables online claim submission for customers/brokers and web-based claims handling for adjusters while maintaining system consistency.]

## Key Elements
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID)
- Token Service (STS)
- Directory & Graph API Component
- B2C / External Identity Federation Gateway
- Audit & Reporting Component
- Azure API Management
- Claims Processing Service (Java, Spring Boot, Azure Container Apps)
- Migration Dashboard (React, Node.js, Azure Container Apps)
- Azure Service Bus
- Azure Logic Apps / Functions
- Azure SQL Database
- Azure Key Vault
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Claims Processing Service validates JWT tokens from Token Service via HTTPS (OIDC metadata/JWKS)
- Azure API Management enforces token validation at the edge using OAuth 2.0 introspection and JWT validation policies
- Azure Application Insights / Log Analytics ingests telemetry from Audit & Reporting Component via HTTPS (Azure Diagnostic Settings)
- Claims Processing Service and Azure API Management consume public JWKS endpoints from Token Service via HTTPS (GET)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) for identity management and SSO (R-07 requirement)
- OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocols for token issuance and validation
- Terraform / Bicep for Infrastructure-as-Code to prevent environment drift
- Azure Application Insights for sign-in and audit telemetry monitoring
- Azure Container Apps hosted on Azure West Europe for modern containerized services

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture utilizes Azure services to safely modernize claims processing while keeping the legacy mainframe as the system of record for 3-year migration safety. This decouples the cloud web applications from expensive mainframe changes while meeting strict consistency and security requirements.]

Azure Application Insights.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous claim processing. It utilizes Azure cloud services integrated with on-premise infrastructure to provide secure, scalable claim submission, adjuster management, and monitored data migration.]

## Key Elements
- Users: Customer, Broker, Claims Adjuster, System Operators / Support Leads
- External Systems: On-premise COBOL/DB2 Legacy Mainframe
- Azure API Management (Azure API Management)
- Claims Processing Service (Java, Spring Boot, Azure Container Apps)
- Migration Dashboard (React, Node.js, Azure Container Apps)
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Service Bus)
- Azure Logic Apps / Functions (Azure Logic Apps, Azure Functions)
- Azure SQL Database (Azure SQL Database, TDS)
- Azure Key Vault (Azure Key Vault)
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) (Azure Active Directory (Entra ID), OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect)
- Azure Application Insights (Azure Application Insights)
- Application Insights SDK / Auto-collection agents
- Log Analytics Workspace (Azure Log Analytics, Kusto Query Language)
- Application Insights Alert Rules (Azure Monitor alerts, Webhook/Action Groups)
- Application Insights Workbooks (Azure Workbooks, JSON/KQL)
- Application Insights Metrics Explorer (Azure Monitor, Time-series DB)

## Relationships
- Customer and Broker interact with Azure API Management via HTTPS (Port 443)
- Claims Adjuster interacts with Migration Dashboard via HTTPS (Port 443)
- Azure API Management routes requests to Claims Processing Service via HTTPS (Port 443)
- Claims Processing Service communicates with Azure Service Bus via AMQP (Port 5671)
- Claims Processing Service persists data in Azure SQL Database via TDS (Port 1433)
- Claims Processing Service and Migration Dashboard authenticate via Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) using OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
- Claims Processing Service and Migration Dashboard send telemetry to Application Insights SDK via HTTPS (Port 443)
- System Operators query Log Analytics Workspace and view Application Insights Workbooks via Azure Portal / HTTPS (Port 443) / KQL

## Technology Stack
- Hybrid Cloud (Azure West Europe & On-Premise Mainframe) chosen to bridge legacy mainframe constraints with modern cloud capabilities.
- Java Spring Boot and React on Azure Container Apps chosen for scalable containerized microservices despite team's low cloud experience.
- Azure SQL Database chosen for managed relational persistence with TDS protocol support.
- Azure Service Bus chosen for reliable asynchronous messaging across the hybrid boundary.
- Azure Application Insights and Log Analytics Workspace chosen for zero-infrastructure APM, distributed tracing, and compliance auditing.
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) chosen for secure Single Sign-On (SSO) and RBAC integration.
- Terraform/Bicep chosen for Infrastructure-as-Code to prevent configuration drift.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture enables the incremental migration of claim types away from the expensive mainframe while strictly adhering to the 3-year coexistence mandate and zero-downtime constraints. Leveraging managed Azure services and robust observability mitigates risks associated with the team's low cloud experience and guarantees zero lost claims.]
